title: How does a microwave heat food?
sources: American Journal of Physics Dielectric Heating

lines.text: Do microwaves heat food from the inside out like everyone always tells you?
lines.caps: Does a microwave heat | food from the *inside | *out?

lines.text: The answer is no, and the actual science is far more fascinating.
lines.caps: The truth is *no | and the science is *wild!

lines.text: Inside the oven, a component called a magnetron generates electromagnetic waves vibrating at two point four gigahertz.
Water, sugar, and fat molecules inside your food are polar, meaning they have positive and negative ends.
lines.caps: Water molecules in *food | have positive and *negative poles

lines.text: As the electric field flips two point four billion times a second, the water molecules violently twist back and forth.
This molecular friction creates intense thermal heat, warming your food from the outer layers inward.
That is why thick burritos can be scalding hot outside and freezing in the center.
lines.caps: Why hot *pockets | are boiling outside and *frozen inside!
